short: Brazil has no AI law in force. Its AI bill, PL 2338/2023, was last read on this site as stalled in the Chamber of Deputies after Senate approval; the LGPD is the binding layer. Brazil's official sites could not be reached on 25 October 2026, so this page is not re-verified.
title: Brazil AI Laws
subtitle: PL 2338/2023, the AI bill, and the LGPD that binds today
body_html:
Status at a glance

AI bill pending; not re-verified. This page carries the site's August 2026 reading of Brazil. On 25 October 2026 the Chamber of Deputies, the Senate, the Planalto legislation site and the data protection authority all refused connections from this crawler, so nothing below could be re-read on an official source, and the page says so rather than presenting it as checked. As last read: PL 2338/2023, the most EU-like AI bill in the Americas, with risk-based classification, prohibited practices, rights to contest AI decisions and impact assessments for high-risk systems, passed the Senate on 10 December 2024 and went to a special committee of the Chamber of Deputies in April 2025, where it awaited the rapporteur's opinion. Until it passes, the binding layer is the General Data Protection Law (LGPD).

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberStage, as last readIn force
AI billPL 2338/2023Senate approval 10 December 2024; Chamber special committee from April 2025No
Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD)Lei 13.709/2018EnactedYes

Who regulates and enforces

  • National Data Protection Authority (ANPD): enforces the LGPD. The bill, as last read, would have it coordinate a national AI governance system.

Scope and reach

No AI statute is in force. The LGPD's scope was not re-read.

Core obligations

  • Today: the LGPD's duties on processing personal data, which reach AI systems that process it.
  • Under the bill, as last read: risk classification, prohibited practices, impact assessments for high-risk systems, and rights to contest AI decisions and to human participation.

Penalties

BreachMaximum, as last readProvisionEnforcer
LGPD infringements2% of the company's revenue in Brazil, capped at BRL 50 million per infraction. Not re-verified on 25 October 2026.LGPD Art. 52ANPD
Under PL 2338/2023, if enactedUp to BRL 50 million or 2% of revenue, as the August 2026 reading stated. Not re-verified.PL 2338/2023Not yet established

What is coming next

  • The rapporteur's opinion in the Chamber's special committee, then a Chamber vote. No date was set when last read; the Chamber's record of the bill is watched weekly and will be read when it answers.

What the Chamber has done since, as reported

Because the official sites refuse this crawler, the following is assembled from Brazilian legal and trade press and is reported, not verified. The Chamber's president Hugo Motta created the special committee in April 2025 and it was installed on 20 May 2025, with Deputy Luísa Canziani (PSD-PR) presiding and Deputy Aguinaldo Ribeiro (PP-PB), who had reported the tax reform, as rapporteur. Ribeiro's work plan of 27 May 2025 scheduled ten thematic public hearings, five regional seminars and an international one before any opinion, with a target of 25 November 2025. That slipped: in December 2025 the committee leadership promised a vote in the first week of February 2026, and by June 2026 the trade press was reporting the vote postponed again, with 2026 being an election year. On whether the rapporteur's opinion has yet been filed, sources read in October 2026 disagree, so this page does not say.

Two things did change. In December 2025 the Executive sent Congress its own bill, PL 6.237/2025, creating the Sistema Nacional de Desenvolvimento, Regulação e Governança de Inteligência Artificial (SIA) with the ANPD as the residual regulator for sectors no other agency covers, supported by the Central Bank, ANVISA, ANATEL and a national council; that bill is attached to PL 2.338 along with 36 others, so the committee is now consolidating 38 texts. And the ANPD published in December 2025 its map of priority themes for 2026 and 2027, which names AI and emerging technologies as one of four enforcement axes, so the authority that would run the SIA is already supervising AI under the LGPD.

The Senate text that the Chamber is working from keeps the EU-style risk tiers, a list of prohibited uses, rights to explanation and human review, impact assessments for high-risk systems, and fines of up to R$ 50 million per infringement. If the Chamber changes it, as the executive bill makes likely, the text returns to the Senate, which has the last word, so sanction by the President is not expected before 2027.

Sources

  • Regulamentação da inteligência artificial no Brasil: estado atual e perspectivas, Barbieri Advogados (secondary)
  • Plano de trabalho da Comissão Especial, 27 May 2025, via Capital Digital
  • PL 2338/2023, legislative record, Câmara dos Deputados (unreachable on 25 October 2026)
  • Lei 13.709/2018 (LGPD), Planalto (unreachable on 25 October 2026)

Last verified

Not re-verified on an official source. The last official reading is the site's of August 2026; on 25 October and 4 November 2026 the Chamber, the Senate, Planalto and the ANPD refused the connection, and this crawler does not route around a refusal. The committee section added on 4 November 2026 rests on the Brazilian press and law-firm notes, which disagree on whether the rapporteur's opinion has been filed.
